goals: Mechanistic: quantify per-column partitioning of precipitation into ET, surface runoff, and sub-surface drainage/recharge across the Naches basin and attribute differences to elevation-driven forcing and soil texture
Validation: compare simulated SWE to SNOTEL, simulated water-table depth to USGS wells (process-level), and flag streamflow validation as blocked

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves the full water balance (ET, runoff, drainage/recharge, snow, soil moisture) at each (lat,lon); spatial sampling spans the basin's heterogeneity. Partitioning is a native per-column output.

answerable: Per-column partitioning of P into ET, surface runoff, and drainage/recharge
Elevation control on partitioning at the ~12 km NLDAS scale (precip/temp/snow vary orographically across columns)
Soil-texture control on partitioning (SSURGO per-column lever)
SWE validation against 6 SNOTEL stations (H2OSNO/SWE simulated and output)
Water-table depth compared to USGS wells as a caveated process check (requires warm start + spin-up)

not_answerable.aspect: Validation of runoff/recharge against the 93 USGS stream gauges
not_answerable.why: Single-column, no lateral transport or routing: the model has no native integrated streamflow at a gage location; per-column runoff cannot be summed to a hydrograph without an aggregation/routing step.

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km elevation contrasts (sharp valley-vs-ridge forcing gradients)
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 at 0.125 deg has no within-cell lapse rate; sub-grid terrain is unresolved, so ridgetop SWE is underestimated and fine elevation gradients are smoothed.

not_answerable.aspect: Regional water-table depth matching well observations exactly
not_answerable.why: No lateral/regional groundwater flow; ELM 1-D equilibrium differs from the real lateral-flow water table, so agreement with wells is only process-level.

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band x dominant soil class), with validation columns pinned to observation sites
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands x ~3 dominant soil classes = ~12 baseline cells; add light replication in the rain-snow transition and valley bottoms (the most partition-sensitive zones) -> 16. Smallest set that spans both drivers while keeping NLDAS runtime (~10x Qian) tractable.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the 1100-1500 m rain-snow transition (snowmelt timing and recharge sensitivity peak here) and in valley bottoms/riparian corridors (strongest recharge and soil-moisture dynamics, and where wells exist). Thin the highest ridge band since sub-12 km forcing under-resolves it.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2x replication within the rain-snow transition and valley strata to separate soil signal from forcing signal within a band; single columns elsewhere.

sampling_plan.reason: Isolates recharge/drainage under high-permeability substrate at basin floor where wells exist for WTD comparison.
Contrasts runoff-vs-recharge partitioning under low-permeability soil at low elevation.
Spans dominant soil classes at intermediate elevation to map ET vs runoff transition.
Isolates snowmelt-driven recharge under fast-draining soil in the most partition-sensitive band.
Captures snowmelt partitioning between runoff and recharge where soil limits infiltration; co-located with SNOTEL for SWE check.
Bounds the snow-dominated, ET-limited end-member; flagged as forcing-under-resolved.
Replication to separate soil-texture effect from elevation/forcing effect within a fixed band.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place/associate columns at the 6 SNOTEL elevations; compare simulated H2OSNO peak and melt-out timing
validation_design.metric: bias and RMSE of peak SWE; melt-out date offset

validation_design.comparison: co-located but process-level — 1-D ELM equilibrium differs from lateral-flow water table; interpret as trend/order-of-magnitude, not exact match; requires WTD-informed warm start + spin-up
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on well data density

validation_design.comparison: BLOCKED — no routing/aggregation; cannot form integrated streamflow from independent columns

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (elevation-resolved), native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start + short spin-up for recharge/WTD states

requires_capabilities.why: Convert per-column surface runoff + drainage into an integrated hydrograph at gage locations
requires_capabilities.blocks: Validation against the 93 USGS stream gauges

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS-2 has no within-cell lapse rate; sharp valley/ridge gradients and ridgetop SWE are under-resolved
requires_capabilities.blocks: Fine-scale elevation attribution and accurate ridgetop SWE

requires_capabilities.capability: WTD-informed warm start + multi-year spin-up execution
requires_capabilities.why: Recharge and water table are slow states; cold start pins WTD at ~8.8 m and reads recharge ~0
requires_capabilities.blocks: Any quantitative recharge or WTD result

requires_capabilities.why: Soil texture is a primary partitioning driver and stratification axis

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL and USGS well observation ingest
requires_capabilities.why: Pin validation columns and compute metrics against measured SWE and WTD
Expand elevation-band placement rules into concrete points within HUC 17030002
1-D columns lack regional/lateral flow; needed for a true water-table comparison to wells

assumptions: Naches is treated as fully within CONUS NLDAS-2 coverage (bbox ~ -121.5..-120.5, 46.4..47.2).
SSURGO provides dominant soil classes spanning coarse/loam/fine within the basin; exact per-point textures are resolved downstream.
USGS wells lie predominantly in valley/lower-mid terrain where the warm start is most meaningful.
Reported partitioning is per-column water balance (ET, surface runoff, drainage/recharge) averaged over a common analysis period within 1980-2018, not a routed basin yield.
Recharge is approximated by ELM sub-surface drainage/recharge flux after warm start + spin-up.
open_questions: How many USGS wells have usable WTD records inside the HUC8, and at what depths?
Which analysis/forcing years should define the partitioning climatology (full 1980-2018 vs a representative wet/dry subset)?
Is a downstream routing/aggregation step planned, which would unlock the 93 gauges for validation?
Are the 6 SNOTEL stations spread across elevation bands or clustered, which affects how they anchor the elevation stratification?
